recipes.name: Southern Pecan Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 recipe pastry for a 9 inch single crust pie

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Whisk eggs gently in a medium bowl just until blended. Whisk in sugar, corn syrup, melted butter, vanilla, and salt, then stir in pecans.
Place the unbaked deep-dish pie crust on a rimmed baking sheet. Pour the filling into the crust.

Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Without removing the pie, reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Continue baking until the edges are set and slightly puffed and the center jiggles gently as one piece, 35 to 40 minutes. If the crust browns too quickly, loosely cover the edges with foil. Let the pie cool on a wire rack before slicing so the filling can set.

raw_recipe.headline: Southern Pecan Pie
raw_recipe.description: This Southern pecan pie has a rich, gooey filling packed with pecans in a flaky crust for an easy Thanksgiving or holiday dessert.

review.reviewBody: Ok once again a southern woman talking. That said I loved this pie !!!! what I loved about it was that it's not tooth ache sweet, it is just right. I used light and dark corn syrup and I think that is what made the difference in the sweetness. Thanks Nikki for a great recipe it will be the only pecan pie I make and will pass it down.

Excellent recipe. This is the one my mother passed down. I now realize that it is the KARO syrup recipe but it is still the way to go. After making many of these pies I have a few suggestions. Use only KARO or other top of the line syrups. Also bring all ingredients to room temperature before mixing. Do not over mix or use electric mixer; this tends to make the pie runny. Another tip - use normal size eggs. Extra large eggs will keep it from setting up. I shield the crust edges for the first 40 minutes, remove for the last 15 minutes. This keeps the crust from becoming too dark before pie is ready. One last thing, I bake mine exactly 55 minutes! No more, no less. I have found this is perfect for my oven which is calibrated correctly. I hope this helps.

I made this pie a cpl times to rave reviews, although it wasn't quite as good as my grandmother's (she was a pie master). 
I specifically recall her using brown sugar so I substituted brown sugar, but this made the pie just too sweet. I decided to use both, 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup brown sugar and the result was a home run!!! I've seen other reviews doing this with the corn syrup.....I may try this in the future, but then again why fix something that isn't broken ??
In addition, I brown/warm the pecans (I add an extra 1/2 cup) in a skillet on the stove top until the natural oils are released. This makes the house smell wonderful and gives the pie a rich, nuttier flavor!!!
It's still not quite my grandmother's, but is equally as delicuous. Everyone raves over this pie and always wants the recipe!!!

I don't like pecan pie but I made it for a funeral this week. My best friend's husband called and wanted to know why I had been keeping to myself all these years - it was the best pie he had ever had. It became 5 stars when I used 1/2 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar as well as 1/2 cup light Karo syrup and 1/2 cup dark Karo syrup. I even saw one guy pick up the pie tin and scrape the bottom. LOL! My husband and I think the secret is to keep cooking it until the center is completely jelled...no longer runny. Put aluminum foil around the pie shell edges so that does not burn.

Awesome recipe!I make 4 of these every Thanksgiving! Use 1/2 cup light and 1/2 cup dark corn syrup. Also added 1 tablespoon of flour to mixture to help with the setting. To prevent your pie from burning, bake at 350 degrees for 50 mins with foil around crust, then remove foil and bake for an additional 10 minutes. Comes out PERFECT every time!

I have been making this pie for years. A few changes like other bakers I used dark and light corn syrup. And a 1/4 cup less sugar. I also chopped my pecans and made the crust by hand. Took about 40 min. Was well worth it!!

This recipe actually make two 9" regular pies or one 9" deep dish pie. I read that some say the pie did not set. You have to use small or medium eggs, any larger, the pie will not set. Also, do not over cook. I prefer my pie to be a medium brown, not dark brown.

great recipe! i tried the half light, half dark syrup suggested in reviews. resulted in 'just right' sweetness. i used fresh pecans and chopped them. as in other reviews, when time is up, check for jiggle in the center. no jiggle, remove from oven. the times were good. would suggest covering the crust with strips of foil until the last 15 minutes. the pie came out wonderful!! will make this again!! UPDATE: first used regular pie crust and it was full! need steady hands! so i tried a deep pie crust and i am going to have to make adjustments....same times as recipe except : cover entire pie loosely and bake another 10-15 min. the times are good, but ovens are different, so just watch for the jiggle and cover if going over original time. will keep making until i run out of pecans in the yard!!!
Very easy and taste great if sautéed 1 cup of pecans with butter in skillet before adding to mix also do half brown sugar and half white sugar. You won’t be disappointed !
I used brown butter and toasted the pecans first. This was a big hit, I’ve been asked to make it for Thanksgiving dessert

I made this for the first time and it got RAVE reviews! It was so easy to make and the only thing I changed, based on another review, was added 1 TBSP. of vanilla. I used 1-1/2 cups of pecans and thought that was plenty. I covered just the edges of the pie crust for the first 45 minutes and then removed the foil and the crust browned nicely. I also didn't remove it from the oven until the middle of the pie didn't "jiggle" anymore and it was perfect. Will make another one today for my Dad's birthday party tomorrow. My family LOVED it and wants more!
The taste was great. Filling was too runny. Let it set for 3 hours on the counter and almost 2 in the fridge. Not sure what happened. Pretty bummed it was a watery mess.
It filled the kitchen with a wonderful aroma and tastes even better.
Great recipe just right amount of everything
Amazing flavor

I will come back and edit how it tastes once I find out after my event tomorrow. I doubled the recipe and ended up with a little filling left over that I will use to make mini pies. I followed the cooking instructions cooking for 15 mins at 400° but then cooked for a remaining 30 minutes at 350°. I placed both pies on cookie sheets and tested the middle with a toothpick. The edges "crisped" some on one piece but nothing that I think will affect the flavor.
Simple and delicious!
I always add a tbsp ap flour because of the humidity in my area. Sets up perfect. This pie is a winner. Ty

I ended up doubling the recipe and using half karo syrup and half Ms. Butterworth's extra buttery maple syrup. I did use salted butter and added salt so it came out on the salty side but it wasn't as salty as salted caramel. It actually came out pretty damn good. Since my pie dishes were deep dish next time I will triple the recipe and not add any salt because the salted butter and the maple syrup has plenty of salt. So try out my tweaks and share how much you enjoyed the slight different flavor. I'm sure if you use a maple flavoring you could get that maple taste but I love Ms. Butterworths syrup that's why I chose to use this syrup instead of flavoring. I love the recipe and you can never add too much butter to this recipe I think I tripled the butter that it calls for in the recipe. I also curled up the edges so it wouldn't overflow just in case. I've had that happen to me in the past. These are my special ideas for a alternate flavors best dessert. Thanks Love @Yesmore23
